metadata.title: CapRover vs Dokku: Open-Source Dashboard and CLI
metadata.description: Compare CapRover and Dokku across simplicity, server requirements, open-source dashboards, deployment, Docker orchestration, NGINX, one-click apps and rollback.

hero.title: Get a complete open-source dashboard without giving up the command line.
hero.intro: CapRover makes the normal path visual and straightforward, while keeping CLI, API, NGINX and Docker controls available when needed. You do not have to choose between ease of use and infrastructure access.
hero.verdict: Choose CapRover when dashboard operations, One-Click Apps, rollback and multi-node orchestration should be included in the open-source product. Consider Dokku when a CLI-first workflow, broad builder selection, cron and a composable plugin system are central requirements.

resourceDescription: Both CapRover and Dokku document a 1 GB minimum with their default Docker-based runtimes. CapRover includes its web dashboard and Docker Swarm model at that published starting requirement.
capabilityTitle: Visual operations and CLI deployment in the same open-source product.

articles.title: The dashboard is the simple path
paragraphs: Domains, certificates, environment variables, persistent directories, replicas, logs and deployment history are visible and editable without assembling commands.
That makes routine operations approachable for every developer who can access the CapRover dashboard.

articles.title: The command line is still there
paragraphs: Run caprover deploy from a local project, upload an archive, deploy an image or trigger a generic Git webhook. The dashboard itself uses CapRover's HTTP API.
CapRover adds a visual workflow without taking away automation or terminal-based deployment.

articles.title: Simple does not mean limited
paragraphs: Most apps use the generated NGINX and Docker configuration unchanged. Advanced workloads can edit the complete per-app NGINX template and override native Docker service settings.
These controls stay out of the common path until an operator deliberately needs them.

articles.title: The practical difference
paragraphs: Dokku's open-source core is intentionally CLI-first and highly composable through builders, commands and plugins. Dokku Pro adds its official web interface and API separately.
CapRover includes its visual operations workflow, One-Click catalog and Swarm management directly in the open-source platform.

caprover: A full web dashboard should be included in the open-source platform.
You want a simple visual workflow and direct local deployment together.
You want deep NGINX and Docker controls available without making them the default workflow.
Docker Swarm clustering and rollback should be managed through the same product.
You rely on a one-click catalog of deployable applications and databases.
competitor: SSH commands and Git push should be the primary interface.
Buildpacks and a composable plugin system are essential.
You need built-in cron task definitions or global environment variables.

migrationDescription: Convert Dokku configuration into CapRover environment variables and application settings, add captain-definition files, map domains, and migrate datastore contents with the database's own backup and restore tools.
